findings.evidence: template/scripts/publication_queue.py diff lines 187-189 (`observed = _pr(...)`, `_comments(...)` inside _transient_wait, called from the `except` branches of _integrate at lines 257/263). Previously these branches returned `waiting` without any network call. A repeated outage may therefore bypass the counter that is meant to bound it.
findings.summary: _transient_wait and _reset_transient perform fresh _pr/_comments reads outside any retry. During the same outage that caused the integration failure, these reads can raise, so a candidate that previously became a plain `waiting` now surfaces as a worker-level QueueError and is skipped as not observable without its counter being incremented.

findings.evidence: _worker_candidate diff lines 246-248 call _reset_transient for every non-merged, non-released outcome; _reset_transient (lines 212-217) reads `_pr` and `_comments` before checking for a non-zero counter.
findings.summary: After every successful non-transient evaluation, _reset_transient does two extra API reads (PR + comments) even when no counter exists. A read failure there is raised after integration work has already completed, so it can fail a healthy candidate.
